newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs up 5 cts but fuel erases gai.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs up 5 cts but fuel erases gai.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Tuesday after some areas of the market lost early gains.
Brent futures fell lower during afternoon trading and slipped some 50 cents a barrel below the days highs.

Brent crude CFDs rose about five cents for this week to 38 cents under June. This compares with levels of around 63 cents under a week ago. The next three weeks also edged higher to 35 cents, 31 cents and 27 cents under respectively.
Gasoline swaps were little changed after falling back from early $2 a tonne gains.

Rotterdam barges traded up to $195.50 for early May in the morning but later dipped to trade at $192 and $193. May swaps traded at $199 to $199.50 by lunchtime before dipping back to talk $197.50 by the close. June talked some $3.50 a tonne lower with July a further $3.50 below June.

Heavy fuel firmed $1 a tonne to talk around $84 for May barges after peaking at $85.50 during the morning. June was 50 cents higher but dealers said the thin physical market had dampened trade. Low sulphur was valued just above $90 for May during the morning but then dipped to $88.
Gas oil against Brent held at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums were flat with May bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
